headline: A US judge sentenced a man to 18 months in prison for using AI-made songs and bots to steal more than $8 million in streaming royalties.
score_reason: First criminal sentence of its kind, but a single case with a sentence below the guideline range.
importance_line: The sentence puts a price on AI-driven streaming fraud that takes money from real artists, though advocates say one case will not stop it.
summary: Billboard reports that Michael Smith, 54, was sentenced in Manhattan federal court on 6 Oct 2026 to 18 months in prison and two years of supervised release for using AI to make thousands of songs and bots to play them billions of times, earning more than $8 million in royalties. Billboard calls it the first criminal conviction over streaming fraud, and the sentence is well below the 46 to 57 months the federal guidelines called for.
